clue.text: Movie star's absurd rage with Bogart

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: something absurd is nonsensical, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A film idol flies into a ridiculous temper with Humphrey Bogart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' signals an anagram of RAGE plus BOGART, which makes the Swedish-born Hollywood actress's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbo was a celebrated Hollywood actress of the silent and early sound era.

clue.text: Fruit available in good time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Some fruit will be ready to eat in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: A gage is a plum, as in greengage.

clue.text: Make money from vessel loaded with tea, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so we want something sounding like the vessel

parts.note: an urn is the large vessel that holds tea at a gathering

explanation.surface: Someone profits by selling from a tea urn.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the R, URN and EARN sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain income through work.

clue.text: Where tour guide begins talking, prior to careful analysis

definitions.meaning: a guide starts speaking at the first place of interest on a tour, the first 'sight'
on an immediate first impression, before thinking it over

explanation.surface: A guide's opening remarks come before any detailed study.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means judging immediately, from a first glance rather than considered study.

clue.text: Anger in an Eastern or Western town

indicators.note: in tells us the word for anger sits inside the word an

parts.note: bile is ill temper or anger

explanation.surface: Rage breaks out in some town, whether east or west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern or Western' looks like a pair of choices, but Eastern only gives E and 'Western town' is the definition: Abilene, Kansas, a cattle town of the Wild West.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilene in Kansas was a famous cow town of the American frontier, where Wild Bill Hickok was marshal.

clue.text: One predicts fatality when female tucks into poison

indicators.note: tucks into means the word for female is placed inside the word for poison

parts.note: bane is an old word for poison, as in henbane

explanation.surface: A woman eats something poisonous, and death is foretold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' suggests eating, but it means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore this spirit wails to foretell a death in the family.

clue.text: Light entertainment

definitions.meaning: pale in colour, as hair or skin can be
a funfair or fete offering rides and stalls

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pale-coloured and an outdoor event with amusements.

clue.text: In a vote, I repeatedly act carelessly, being Monday's soluti this?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'In a vote, I repeatedly act carelessly, being Monday's soluti this?': OCR garble in the definition; wordplay is A POLL around an anagram of I I ACT, but the defining words are lost
annotationWithheld.clue: In a vote, I repeatedly act carelessly, being Monday's soluti this?

clue.text: HIE Repeating a novel, B A arrange text differently

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An author repeats a novel and has the pages laid out again.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held carries OCR debris ('HIE', 'B A'); the clue proper reads 'Repeating a novel, arrange text differently'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaginate is to renumber or reflow the pages of a document.

clue.text: Validate, when divided, for example

parts.note: split the first word into 'Val, I date': Val, the woman I go out with, is an instance of the kind of person meant

explanation.surface: Something is confirmed, once it is split up, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Validate' looks like a verb to define, but broken up it reads 'Val I date', and 'for example' says Val is one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman someone is dating, such as Val here, is a romantic partner of that kind.

clue.text: Joe badly treated in TV series

definitions.meaning: A British name for a put-upon person landed with the unpleasant jobs
a long-running domestic drama on television

explanation.surface: Someone called Joe is mistreated in a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Soap is British slang for an ordinary dupe who gets imposed upon; Chambers defines it so.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial drama; the dupe sense comes from the slang name Joe Soap.

clue.text: Main character in book made into film nobody sees

definitions.text: Main character in book made into film nobody sees

parts.words: Main character in book made into film nobody sees
parts.note: H. G. Wells's novel about a scientist rendered unseen was filmed in 1933; its hero cannot be seen, even on screen

explanation.surface: A protagonist from a filmed novel whom no audience watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nobody sees' suggests a flop film, but it means the character cannot be seen at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells's title character, Griffin, has made himself unseeable.

clue.text: Release fine monarch not bound by orthodox beliefs

explanation.surface: Let a fine ruler go, as he is no longer tied to doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms opinions independently of religious or other dogma.

clue.text: Meals taste awful, hence deadlocks

indicators.note: awful marks the letters as badly put together, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The food is disgusting, so negotiations stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation where neither side can make progress, as in chess.

clue.text: It may be provided with table for N C consumer's digital M M input

annotationWithheld.clue: It may be provided with table for N C consumer's digital M M input

clue.text: National emblem that's blown down, to begin with

definitions.text: National emblem that's blown down, to begin with

parts.words: National emblem that's blown down, to begin with
parts.note: Scotland's plant symbol forms the first part of the name of the fluffy seeds that drift on the wind

explanation.surface: A country's symbol was knocked over at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown down' suggests toppled, but it points to thistledown, whose start is this plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is Scotland's floral emblem, and its feathery seeds are thistledown.

clue.text: Version of text inciting rebellion after deposing leader

indicators.note: the leader deposed means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: sedition is speech or conduct stirring rebellion against authority

explanation.surface: A book's new version stirs revolt once the ruler is toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposing leader' fits the rebellion story, but removes the first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one particular printing or form of a published work.

clue.text: Cutting down or adding to record collection

definitions.meaning: entering details in a log or record

explanation.surface: Felling trees, or adding to a pile of vinyl albums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record collection' suggests music, but it means a log being kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the timber trade and writing entries in a journal.

clue.text: Authentic parts that could be arranged for ingénue

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Real roles that might be set up for a young actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Something genuine is real and not fake.

clue.text: I used in class some pictures from computer

indicators.note: used in means the letter is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
part means some, as in a portion

explanation.surface: Someone shows a class images taken from a PC.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip art is ready-made graphics supplied for use in documents.

clue.text: Was obsequious, so got along swimmingly?

definitions.meaning: moved through water using the front-crawl stroke

explanation.surface: Someone toadied, and so got on well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmingly' usually means smoothly, but here it is literal swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both fawned and swam front crawl.

clue.text: Two kinds of seamen easy to until of

annotationWithheld.clue: Two kinds of seamen easy to until of

clue.text: One article, or a couple

definitions.meaning: a single thing in a list
two people in a romantic relationship, said to be one of these

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a single object and, informally, a pair who are dating.

clue.text: Symbol it's fashionable to have around company

indicators.note: to have around means the fashionable word encloses the company abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sign that it is trendy to entertain guests.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a representative image or emblem.

clue.text: Assumed it's removed

definitions.meaning: adopted, as a role or duty, in the past tense
carried off or withdrew something from a place, in the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone presumed the thing had been taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense covers both taking on a role and taking something away.

clue.text: I impact old characters in way that's tactful

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, are set in a new way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to influence elderly people in a gentle manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being diplomatic means handling people with sensitivity and discretion.

clue.text: It's kept in cellar, as last resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again into a new order

explanation.surface: Something stored in a wine cellar, to be used only in desperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last resort' reads as a stock phrase, but 'resort' is re-sort, an anagram of LAST. The cellar is a salt cellar, not a wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt cellar is the small dish or shaker holding table seasoning.

clue.text: Star conductor

definitions.meaning: the principal male actor in a production
one who guides or leads others

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the principal actor and, literally, a man who leads the way.
